title: Appliance-led VPC Onboarding: progressive reveal flows, modular screenshots, and upgrade continuity
creator: Marta Chen
description:
Problem: Customers installing the appliance or private VPC frequently get overwhelmed by single-view setup screens. They ask for clearer progressive disclosure, fewer jumps between installer and console screenshots, and a visible upgrade path in the onboarding flow.

Goal: Produce a modular set of visual assets (microcopy, progressive-reveal screenshot frames, and upgrade continuity panels) that can be used in the Private/VPC quickstart guide, in-product first-run flows, and the release notes. The assets should support both: (1) an operator-led appliance flow (local console + serial/USB first-boot) and (2) a cloud-provisioned VPC flow, with consistent visual language and microcopy.

Scope: 12 high-fidelity screenshot compositions (desktop + narrow widths for docs), 6 progressive reveal overlays that show staged steps (networking, routing, secrets/KMS, node join), 4 upgrade continuity frames illustrating preflight checks and rollback affordances, and a concise microcopy pack (CTA/alert/tooltip strings).

Constraints & assumptions: Must reuse existing brand tokens (typography, color) from Figma library v2. No new icons unless approved by brand. Screenshots should be producible from staging environment (staging-console.redwood) to avoid synthetic UI divergence. Security review required for any copy that suggests key management actions.
acceptance_criteria: 12 high-fidelity screenshot compositions exported as PNG and 2x PNGs for retina
Progressive reveal overlays available as transparent SVGs and editable Figma frames
Upgrade continuity panels explain preflight, rolling upgrade, and rollback with copy and visuals
Screenshots validated with engineering against staging console and smoke-tested in the quickstart doc
Stakeholder sign-off from PM (Lena Ortiz) and Eng lead (Diego Morales) recorded in comments
